scope: Persistent Polymarket live Fast/Cancel I/O actors and strategy/completion idle wakes; production deployment pending

environment.transitive_versions: benchmark.Cargo.lock, copied from SDK Cargo.lock and pruned by Cargo

source_findings: Tokio current_thread Handle::spawn allocates a task, binds it through OwnedTasks list shards and pushes remote tasks through Mutex<Synced> injection; single-thread runtime does not remove these locks.
Notify/async channel waking a spawned Tokio task still uses remote task scheduling; spawn_local or FuturesUnordered per request alone does not eliminate all per-request task/node allocation.
Crossbeam SyncWaker register/unregister and notify with waiters lock a mutex. The affected ready queues were lock-free but idle strategy select and completion recv registered waiters.
The previous live auth-to-task audit interval includes strings, allocation, scheduling, wake syscalls and OS preemption; it does not uniquely attribute its entire tail to a lock.

ownership_and_backpressure.io_actor: One startup-boxed Future per physical Fast/Cancel owner; polled by existing hexbot-async-ord CPU 2 root future. No new production OS threads.
ownership_and_backpressure.registry: Fixed 256 actor capacity, startup-only registration; sole writer is I/O root. Saturation fails startup; completed/failed actors release reservations.
ownership_and_backpressure.io_mailbox: Capacity 2; physical connection owner admits one business request at a time. FIFO owned command transfer. Full/stopped queue returns typed NotSent without spawn fallback.
ownership_and_backpressure.completion: Two startup slots per trade route, one reply each, futex wake. Reuse requires all endpoint and timing-generation references to be released. Actor teardown drops outstanding reply guards.
ownership_and_backpressure.strategy_inboxes: Direct private, execution, and market capacities remain 10000 per strategy; venue private FIFO remains 4096; history remains 8. One receiver/strategy thread, shared startup-bound futex hint. No idle Crossbeam select.
ownership_and_backpressure.priority: Admission state, control, direct private, venue private, execution lifecycle, history, then market. A reserved/unpublished lifecycle head blocks market processing. Startup pause, quarantine and replay acknowledgements are retained.
ownership_and_backpressure.overflow: Private/execution envelopes remain retained in existing bounded recovery/router outboxes. Cold timed sends retain their exact value on full/close. Quote snapshots keep existing coalescing policy.
ownership_and_backpressure.wake_protocol: arm -> recheck all priorities -> futex wait -> recheck all priorities. Admission/watchdog fallback polling remains bounded by the existing 10us ceiling.
ownership_and_backpressure.identity: Immutable account/instance labels prepared at lane binding; per-request commands retain context by Arc. Client attempt/generation and audit timestamps stay attached to the request.

benchmark.io_order: old/new/new/old, each with bursts 1 and 6; 24 startup actors on new path; 1200 warmup messages, 100000 measured messages per case
benchmark.idle_order: old/new/new/old, 100 warmup messages then 20000 measured messages per case; 50us producer sleep outside measurement before each send

boundaries.before_publish_to_return: Instant immediately before spawn/try_send through return; includes wake and scheduling/preemption on producer
boundaries.before_publish_to_consume: Same Instant through first consumer instruction after task start or mailbox receive; excludes signing, HTTP, response and strategy work

benchmark.queue_measurement: inflight_high_water is the enforced maximum burst window, not an instrumented Tokio internal queue depth; new per-actor mailbox capacity 2; idle queue capacity 1; all measured retries/drops 0
benchmark.allocation_measurement: Thread-local counting System allocator enabled only around producer publication, startup excluded
limitations: Synthetic handoff benchmark, not live market-receipt-to-first-write latency.
Ordinary scheduling on CPU 0-1 leaves P999/max vulnerable to IRQ/background work; no claim that all maximums improve.
Futex publication is cheaper, but receive-tail results overlap or reverse between runs; isolated live P99/P999 benefit remains unproven.
Preliminary non-locked-transitive run is retained separately; locked run is the primary comparison.

remaining_migration: Legacy/cold compatibility calls retain per-call spawn; live physical Fast/Cancel owners bind persistent lanes before accepting commands.
HTTP/header/signature allocations, downstream transport synchronization, account ownership migration, and same-core Fast preparation serialization remain separate profiling work.
Keep-warm/repair and cold HTTP still use Tokio tasks on their existing runtime ownership.
Deploy through the existing restart script and compare market receipt -> dispatch -> first write plus private application before attributing a live end-to-end tail improvement.
